items.title: Multipartitions with fixed component cores are cyclotomic Jantzen-connected
items.statement: Under the arbitrary-field finite-e nondegenerate cyclotomic hypotheses of [[lem-cyclotomic-jantzen-equivalence-is-schur-and-hecke-block-linkage]], any two $\ell$-multipartitions of a common rank $n$ with equal componentwise $e$-cores are $J$-equivalent, even if their component sizes differ. At fixed component sizes, the full-level coefficient for a change in a single component equals its level-one coefficient. The proof consumes the actual native21 same-e-core Hecke Specht-block theorem for all ranks, not its readiness receipt, and imports no Carter-partition classification.
items.strategy:
Fix the rank n and charges in the Statement. First suppose the component sizes agree. For a single component a of rank m, the actual level-one Hecke algebra is the finite Hecke algebra by [[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]. Its same-core Specht-block clause [[cor-type-a-hecke-specht-modules-are-in-the-same-block-iff-their-labels-have-the-same-e-core]], together with [[lem-cyclotomic-jantzen-equivalence-is-schur-and-hecke-block-linkage]] at level one, connects any two rank-m partitions with equal core by level-one Jantzen edges. The Dipper–James to Murphy convention change is conjugate-dual; core equality is preserved because core(transpose λ)=transpose(core λ). Thus the exact existing clause applies over the original F without an algebraic-closure hypothesis. Rank m=0 has a single empty partition and needs no block theorem.

For two full multipartitions that differ only in component a, every contributing equal-remainder hook pair in J lies in a. The common residue factor Q_a t^(na) is a unit of O. Replacing it by the level-one factor Q_a t^m also multiplies each foot difference by a Laurent unit. Hence its valuation is unchanged, and the full-level J coefficient is exactly the level-one coefficient. Insert the level-one paths in a and leave the other components fixed. Changing the components one at a time connects all equal-size-component multipartitions with the same component cores.

If component weights differ, choose a component whose weight exceeds its target and one whose weight is deficient. A positive-weight component has a removable e-hook, by its core construction. Wrap an e-hook in the deficient component with the same foot residue: for any prescribed foot residue f, moving the lowest bead on runner f−1 down by e creates such a hook, since its foot residue is the starting beta position plus1. The changed components determine the removed/added hook pair uniquely. In the appropriate dominance orientation their J contribution is one signed valuation, with no cancellation. Equal foot residue means its nonzero generic difference is divisible by t−1, so the valuation is a positive integer. Nonzero generic foot differences are part of the exact J formula supplier [[thm-cyclotomic-schur-jantzen-sum-formula-from-rim-hook-valuations]]; no unit-difference or characteristic-zero restriction is inserted. Thus the transfer is a Jantzen edge. It lowers the sum of squares of discrepancies of component hook weights by at least2. Finitely many such transfers equalize component weights. The preceding fixed-size argument then completes the connection. Every moved e-hook preserves the component core, and all steps preserve total rank.

items.title: Cyclotomic multipartitions have equal residue content exactly when Jantzen-connected
items.statement: Let $F$ be any field, $q_H\in F^\times$ have finite order $e\ge2$ with $q_H\ne1$, let $\ell\ge1$ and $Q_a=q_H^{c_a}$. For all $\ell$-multipartitions $\lambda,\mu$ of rank $n\ge0$, the node-residue contents $C_i(\lambda)=\#\{(r,s,a)\in[\lambda]:c_a+s-r\equiv i\pmod e\}$ agree for every $i\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ iff $\lambda\sim_J\mu$ for the exact integer Jantzen coefficients of [[thm-cyclotomic-schur-jantzen-sum-formula-from-rim-hook-valuations]]. This includes arbitrary levels and all field characteristics.
items.strategy:
**Given:** [[thm-cyclotomic-schur-jantzen-sum-formula-from-rim-hook-valuations]] for the actual rim-hook coefficients, [[lem-charged-core-height-matrices-have-content-preserving-descent-and-minimal-switch-connectivity]] for charged core matrices/hubs, and [[lem-fixed-component-core-multipartitions-are-cyclotomic-jantzen-connected]] for fixed-core lifts.

Necessity is elementary. If J_(λµ)≠0, at least one term of its signed integer sum has nonzero valuation. Evaluating its generic foot difference at t=1 therefore gives zero, so the two foot eigenvalues coincide. Since q_H has order e, their charged foot residues agree. The hooks have equal lengths and the same remainder diagram. Along a rim strip, reading from its lowest-left node to its highest-right node increases content by one at every step, so its residue multiset consists of h consecutive residues starting at its foot. Thus the two removed hooks have identical residue counts, proving C(λ)=C(µ). Transitivity gives necessity for every Jantzen path.

For sufficiency let κ be the componentwise core of a member of the rank-n content class. Its size is at most n and is congruent to n modulo e. All such cores have the same hub. The core-matrix lemma gives a sequence of γ=2 zero-size switches followed, unless already minimum, by a γ≥3 strict descent. Every intermediate core has size≤n and the same hub, so adding (n−core-size)/e e-hooks produces a rank-n multipartition of the same content by the equal-hub/equal-size clause.

The following explicit one-hook lift supplies a Jantzen edge across every oriented core switch.

This section is a local combinatorial proof; its Jantzen interpretation uses the exact declared local formula.

Let κ' be obtained from κ by the oriented switch in rows i,j and components a,b above, with γ≥2. Then |κ'|=|κ|−eD, D=γ−2≥0. Write

u=i+etᵢₐ, v=j+e(tⱼₐ+1), v'=j+etⱼ_b, u'=i+e(tᵢ_b+1).

In component a, the core switch removes bead u and inserts v. In component b it removes bead v' and inserts u'. Let w=(n−|κ|)/e≥0. Form λ by moving the lowest bead u of κ's i-runner in component a to u+ew (adding w e-hooks on this runner). Form μ from κ' by moving its lowest bead v on the j-runner in component a to v+e(w+D). Both have size n, the same hub, and hence equal content.

Their beta sets in component a differ only by replacing u+ew with v+e(w+D); those in component b differ only by replacing v' with u'. Since

(v−u)+(u'−v')=−eD,

we have v+e(w+D)−(u+ew)=v'−u'. Thus the two components exchange a single rim hook of length |v'−u'|. This length is nonzero because i≠j modulo e. If v'−u'>0, component b unwraps and a wraps a hook with foot residue i+1 modulo e; if it is negative, a unwraps and b wraps a hook with foot residue j+1 modulo e. In both cases the hook feet have equal residues. The hook pair is uniquely determined because distinct components change, so J's signed valuation is a nonzero integer; there is no cancellation. Hence λ and μ are Jantzen-connected by one edge. This supplies the detail abbreviated in Lyle–Mathas Lemma 3.11.

The generic difference in that unique hook contribution is nonzero by the J supplier, and its specialization vanishes because the charged feet agree, so its positive integer valuation cannot disappear by reduction modulo char F. The fixed-core lemma permits replacing arbitrary lifts by these chosen lifts before and after each switch. Strict descent lowers the nonnegative core size by at least e; therefore it terminates at a minimum core. All minimum cores have equal size and, by the matrix lemma, are connected by γ=2 switches, whose rank-n lifts are connected by the same explicit hook construction. Hence every member of the content class is Jantzen-connected to every other. The empty rank has only one multipartition and is immediate. No affine-center or primitive-block theorem has entered the proof.

items.title: Central content sectors are zero or primitive cyclotomic Hecke blocks
items.statement: Let F be any field and q_H∈F× have finite quantum characteristic e≥2. Use the standard cyclotomic type-A Hecke presentation, level ℓ=Σ_iλ_i≥0, imposed on the FIRST polynomial variable, with λ_i≥0 and I=Z/eZ. For q_H≠1 the roots are q_H^i and q_H has order e; for q_H=1, char F=e>0 and the roots are the prime-field residues i. Use only the early central CRT notation of [[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]] and [[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-polynomial-spectra-and-central-content-sectors]]. For every content α of rank d, eα=Σ_(word contentα)e(word) is either zero or a primitive central idempotent. The nonzero eα are exactly all primitive central idempotents, so H_d^Λ=⊕_α eαH_d^Λ is precisely the block decomposition. At d=0 the unique sector is F, regardless of level; at d>0,ℓ=0 the algebra is zero. This is an arbitrary-level result over the original field in both branches.
items.strategy:
**Given:** the early central-content notation [[def-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sector-notation]] and finite split spectral/central-sector lemma [[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-polynomial-spectra-and-central-content-sectors]], with q_H of finite quantum characteristic e, arbitrary F and dominant cyclotomic multiplicities λ_i. These give central pairwise-orthogonal content idempotents summing to1 and the regular/module CRT interpretation. Their construction asserts no primitivity.

At rank0 the algebra is F, the empty-word projector is1, and this is its unique primitive central idempotent. At positive rank and level0 the defining polynomial is1, so the algebra is0 and every content sector is0; there are no nonzero blocks. Hence assume rank d≥1 and level ell≥1.

In the degenerate branch q_H=1, necessarily char F=e>0. [[lem-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-center-is-the-symmetric-polynomial-image]] gives the full symmetric-polynomial center over this F; [[lem-symmetric-polynomial-centers-have-primitive-split-content-idempotents]] now applies to the early CRT projectors and proves their content sums zero or primitive. This uses neither a field extension nor a power-sum generation assertion.

In the nondegenerate branch q_H≠1 choose a charge list c_1,...,c_ell that repeats each i exactly λ_i times, so Q_a=q_H^(c_a) and the first polynomial is unchanged. The actual arbitrary-level Murphy cellular basis and finite cellular head lemma supply all simple H_d^Lambda-modules as nonzero Specht quotients D^λ. The content-triangular JM helper [[lem-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-murphy-jm-action-is-content-triangular]] says every word on S^λ, and hence on its quotient D^λ, has the node-content C(λ). Thus a simple module in a nonzero eα sector has a label λ with C(λ)=α.

Any two simple modules in that sector have labels with equal content. The actual local finite-e theorem [[thm-cyclotomic-multipartitions-of-fixed-content-are-jantzen-connected]] connects the labels by integer Jantzen edges, and [[lem-cyclotomic-jantzen-equivalence-is-schur-and-hecke-block-linkage]] transfers this to a common Hecke block. If eα decomposed into two nonzero orthogonal central idempotents u,v, the nonzero finite algebras uH and vH would each have a simple module: select a proper right ideal of maximal dimension, which exists because the finite-dimensional possible dimensions have a maximum. The resulting simple modules cannot lie in one block, since the central u acts as identity on the first and zero on the second; all modules and extensions split by u. This contradicts the preceding one-block assertion. Therefore eα is primitive.

Finally in either branch, if b is any primitive central idempotent, write b=Σα b eα. The terms are central orthogonal idempotents, so precisely one is nonzero and b=b eα. Primitivity of the nonzero eα then gives b=eα. Thus every block arises from one and only one nonzero content sum. All sums are finite, field characteristic never reduces an integer K0 adjacency, and no original ResidueDefinition(iv), affine-block classification, or citation-only center theorem is consumed.

items.title: Residue-sequence idempotents and cyclotomic Hecke blocks
items.statement:
Use the charged finite-e field conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]]. By [[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-polynomial-spectra-and-central-content-sectors]], H^Λ_d is finite-dimensional and each minimal polynomial of z_r=X_r (NG) or x_r (DG) splits over c_i=q_H^i or i·1_F. Let ε_r(i) be its canonical CRT primary idempotent (zero for an absent root), and e(ν)=∏_r ε_r(ν_r). On every finite H-module it projects onto the joint generalized residue space. These mutually orthogonal idempotents sum to1. At content α put e_α=Σ_(ν∈I_α)e(ν); it is central, and H^Λ_d is the direct sum of its central ideals H^Λ_α=e_αH^Λ_d=e_αH^Λ_de_α. By [[thm-cyclotomic-hecke-central-content-sectors-are-zero-or-primitive-blocks]], every nonzero e_α is primitive, so every nonzero H^Λ_α is an actual block. This rich block claim is proved, not retained as an unused citation.

At level one Λ=Λ_j, the polynomial generators correspond under the explicit finite-Hecke inverse to X_r=q_H^j(1+(q_H−1)L_r) in NG and x_r=j+L_r in DG, where L_r is the ordinary additive JM element. Thus on a standard tableau node of content m their eigenvalues are q_H^(j+m) and j+m; L_r itself has additive q-content [m]_(q_H). The nonzero joint projectors are precisely the residue words of standard tableaux, and grouping those words by content gives the block labels. At rankzero the empty projector is1 and the unique block is F; at levelzero positive rank all projectors and blocks are zero.
items.strategy: Finite/split spectrum and CRT sums are the declared early lemma, proved independently of basis independence and primitivity by direct global intertwiners and determinant/adjugate annihilators. The separately declared unified primitivity theorem supplies both arbitrary-field branches: NG uses actual Schur/Jantzen/core connectivity, DG uses the proved symmetric-JM center and nilpotent augmentation argument. The level-one JM formulas follow from the independently constructed inverse, with the factor q_H^j and the additive-versus-multiplicative distinction explicit. The ordinary JM cell action is triangular on every field. Filtering the regular algebra by its Murphy cell layers shows a word projector is nonzero exactly when it occurs on a standard-tableau word: the primary-projector functor is exact, each cell layer is the corresponding cell module tensor its finite free left-index space, and every diagonal word occurs in that cell module's finite triangular filtration. This does not require semisimplicity or nonzero cell heads. Every retained block/eigenvalue claim therefore has an actual local supplier; the primitive theorem never supplies its own early CRT/BK prerequisites.

Then the homomorphisms $ho:R^\Lambda_\alpha	o H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[lem-hecke-intertwiners-produce-local-klr-generators]] and $\sigma:H^\Lambda_\alpha	o R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[lem-cyclotomic-klr-block-satisfies-the-hecke-relations]] are mutually inverse $F$-algebra isomorphisms. Equivalently, $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is generated by the Khovanov-Lauda generators $\{e(i)\}\cup\{y_r\}\cup\{\psi_r\}$ subject only to the relations (1.6)-(1.15), and the isomorphism is normalised by $ho(e(i))=e(i)$ and $ho(y_re(i))=(1-q^{-i_r}X_r)e(i)$ if $q
e1$, resp. $ho(y_re(i))=(x_r-i_r)e(i)$ if $q=1$. The degenerate ($q=1$, $\operatorname{char}F=e$) and nondegenerate ($q
e1$) cases are proved separately and both hold in finite quantum characteristic $e$.

items.title: Cyclotomic Hecke blocks inherit a nontrivial Z-grading
items.statement: In the situation of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]], each fixed choice of admissible local normalising series transports the KLR homogeneous decomposition to a Z-grading on H^Λ_α. This is the unique grading for those fixed generator images with deg e(i)=0, deg y_r=2 and deg ψ_r e(i)=−a_(i_r,i_(r+1)). Different admissible series choices give graded-isomorphic transported algebras via ρ′∘ρ^(-1); their underlying identity map need not be graded. The grading can be nontrivial, but it may be trivial on an individual block, including the one-dimensional level-one rank-two e=3 blocks. The ordinary Hecke presentation always has the trivial assignment of degree zero to all its generators. The transported grading is generally expressed using the nilpotent dots and local crossings; ordinary Hecke generators can be sums of different homogeneous pieces, and may be homogeneous in special cases. No claim forbids the degree-zero assignment or asserts every block grading is nontrivial.
items.strategy: Transport each homogeneous summand of R^Λ_α through its fixed algebra isomorphism ρ. Products retain degree addition because ρ is an algebra map. Generator images span the algebra, so their assigned homogeneous degrees determine every degree summand and give uniqueness for that choice. If ρ′ uses another admissible series, ρ′ρ^(-1) sends each homogeneous native generator image to the corresponding new image and hence is graded by construction; no series unit is assumed homogeneous of degree zero. Setting all ordinary Hecke generator degrees to zero makes every relation homogeneous, so the old impossibility assertion is false. One-dimensional sectors have only degree zero (their unit is degree zero and they equal F). For a concrete nontrivial case at level one, e=2, rank two, only word (0,1) survives: first-strand exponent zero kills (1,0), on word(0,0), the equal-color mixed identities give ψ_1 y_2=1 with ψ_1²=0, hence ψ_1=0 after left multiplication by ψ_1, then1=0; so that equal-color sector is zero, y_1=0 and the crossing is zero. The quadratic double-edge relation gives y_2^2=0. Conversely e(0,1)=1,y_2=t,y_1=ψ_1=0 in F[t]/(t^2) satisfy all rank-two relations, so that sector is F[t]/(t^2) with deg t=2. Its BK image supplies an actual nontrivial transported grading, including the characteristic-two degeneration. This example is a witness that the construction can be nontrivial, not a claim about all sectors.

items.title: The homogeneous degree check for the corrected KLR braid relation
items.statement: In the specialized cyclotomic KLR algebra of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the grading $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_r,i_{r+1}}$, fix a triple $i=(i_r,i_{r+1},i_{r+2})$ and put $d(i):=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}-a_{i_ri_{r+2}}-a_{i_{r+1}i_{r+2}}$ (the degree of both three-crossing words $\psi_r\psi_{r+1}\psi_re(i)$ and $\psi_{r+1}\psi_r\psi_{r+1}e(i)$, computed on the successive permuted colour pairs). Then both sides of (1.15) are homogeneous of degree $d(i)$ and the correction term has the same degree: it is $\pm1$ (degree $0$) when $i_{r+2}=i_r\to i_{r+1}$ or $i_{r+2}=i_r\leftarrow i_{r+1}$, it is $y_r+y_{r+2}-2y_{r+1}$ (degree $2$) when $i_{r+2}=i_r\rightleftarrows i_{r+1}$ (the $e=2$ double edge), and it is $0$ otherwise. In particular the single-edge corrected braid relations have degree $0$ and the $e=2$ double-edge corrected braid relation has degree $2$; both match the two sides.
items.strategy: Substitute the cyclic Cartan entries ($a_{mm}=2$, $a_{m,m\pm1}=-1$ for $e\ge3$, $a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$ for $e=2$) into the degree of the words: the three crossings of $\psi_r\psi_{r+1}\psi_re(i)$ cross the colour pairs $(i_r,i_{r+1})$, $(i_r,i_{r+2})$, $(i_{r+1},i_{r+2})$ of the successive permuted sequences, so the degree is the displayed $d(i)$; the other braid word has the same multiset of pairs. Case check: (a) $i_{r+2}=i_r\to i_{r+1}$: $d(i)=-(-1)-2-(-1)=0$ and the correction is $+1$; (b) $i_{r+2}=i_r\leftarrow i_{r+1}$: $d(i)=0$ and the correction is $-1$; (c) $e=2$, $i_{r+2}=i_r\rightleftarrows i_{r+1}$: $a_{i_ri_{r+1}}=a_{i_{r+1}i_{r+2}}=-2$, $a_{i_ri_{r+2}}=a_{00}=2$, so $d(i)=2+2-2=2$, matching the degree $2$ of $y_r+y_{r+2}-2y_{r+1}$; (d) all other cases have correction $0$. The degrees are those of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], and the case list is the source's (1.15). No choice is used. The displayed source word order is ψ_rψ_(r+1)ψ_r−ψ_(r+1)ψ_rψ_(r+1); it equals the native opposite-order τ difference under ψ=−τ. The nonzero correction requires equal outer colors; zero corrections remain homogeneous without asserting their degree is zero.

items.title: The degenerate level-one Hecke-KLR map for S_3
items.statement: Work over $F=\mathbb F_3$ with $q=1$ (so $e=3$), $\Lambda=\Lambda_0$ (level one) and $d=3$: then $H^\Lambda_3\cong \mathbb F_3S_3$ and exactly one block is nonzero, namely $\alpha=\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\alpha_2$ with $e_\alpha=1$. The residue sequences realised by standard tableaux all have residue multiset $\{0,1,2\}$. The degenerate KLR generators are the elements $y_r=\sum_i(x_r-i_r)e(i)$ with $x_r$ the Jucys-Murphy elements of $\mathbb F_3S_3$ (so $x_1=0$, $x_2=(12)$, $x_3=(13)+(23)$), and $\psi_r=\sum_i\varphi_rq_r(i)^{-1}e(i)$ with $\varphi_r=s_r+p_r(i)$ and $p_r(i)=(i_r-i_{r+1}+y_r-y_{r+1})^{-1}$ on unequal components. In this block the mixed relations $\psi_1y_2e(i)=y_1\psi_1e(i)+e(i)$ for $i_1=i_2$ and $\psi_1y_2e(i)=y_1\psi_1e(i)$ for $i_1\ne i_2$, and the quadratic relation $\psi_1^2e(i)=(y_2-y_1)e(i)$ for $i_1\to i_2$, are explicit identities in the six-dimensional algebra $\mathbb F_3S_3$.
items.strategy:
Let c=(12), s=(23), a=(13), and C=c+a+s in F_3S_3. Group multiplication gives C²=0 and Cc=Cs=1+(123)+(132). Put e_+=(1+c)/2 and e_-=(1−c)/2 (2 is invertible in F_3). These are the actual joint CRT projectors e(0,1,2),e(0,2,1): x_1=0,x_2=c,x_3=C−c, so y_1=y_2=0 and y_3=C. All other words vanish. Both projectors are nonzero by the group basis. The full center has basis1,C,1+(123)+(132), with square-zero augmentation ideal spanned by the last two elements; hence it has no nontrivial idempotent and there is one block. This also follows from the declared primitive-content theorem.
For the explicit source3.30 choices, ψ_1=0. On e_+, p_2=−1+C and q_2=−1; on e_-, p_2=1+C and q_2=1. Thus ψ_2e_+=(1−s−C)e_+ and ψ_2e_-=(s+1+C)e_-. Direct group multiplication, c²=s²=1 and csc=scs give ψ_2e_+=e_-ψ_2, ψ_2e_-=e_+ψ_2, ψ_2²e_+=Ce_+, ψ_2²e_-=−Ce_-, and Cψ_2=ψ_2C=0. These are the claimed mixed and quadratic identities with y_3=C,y_2=0. First-crossing mixed identities are zero on every surviving unequal-color word; equal-first-color words are absent, so the universal equal-color formula also holds. The explicit six group elements give the dimension6; no primitive-block citation or Hecke-basis dimension loop is hidden.

e-1$ for a primitive cube root in characteristic $
e3$). Hence there are exactly two nonzero one-dimensional blocks, and their labels are computed from the polynomial generator: on the trivial module $X_1=q^0=1$ and $X_2=q^{-1}T_1X_1T_1=q^{-1}q^2=q$, giving residue sequence $(0,1)$; on the sign module $X_1=1$ and $X_2=q^{-1}(-1)^2=q^{-1}=q^2$, giving $(0,2)$ - equivalently the q-contents of the standard tableaux of $(2)$ and $(1,1)$ ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]). Every nonzero block contains at least one such idempotent, so the remaining four are zero. No choice is used.

items.title: The whole affine Hecke algebra is not one cyclotomic KLR block
items.statement: For a fixed content-block isomorphism, replacing one side by the whole affine algebra, or by the whole cyclotomic quotient in the example below, fails. This does not forbid summing all the central-sector isomorphisms on BOTH sides: (i) the affine Hecke algebra $H_1$ is $F[x_1^{\pm1}]$ resp. $F[x_1]$, hence infinite dimensional, while every cyclotomic block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is finite dimensional of dimension $\le\ell^dd!$; (ii) even after imposing the cyclotomic relation, a single residue-content idempotent $e_\alpha$ cuts out a proper factor: at level one with $d=2$, $e=3$ and $q$ a primitive cube root, $H^\Lambda_2\cong H_{F,q}(S_2)\cong F\times F$ has two nonzero blocks $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}$ and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_2}$, so $H^\Lambda_2$ is not isomorphic to either one of them, and on the KLR side $R^\Lambda_2=R^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}\oplus R^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_2}$ is not isomorphic to a single block.
items.strategy: At rankone the affine presentation is the Laurent polynomial ring F[X_1^(±1)] in NG and polynomial ring F[x_1] in DG. Distinct powers are linearly independent, so each is infinite-dimensional. Charged cyclotomic quotients and their sectors are finite by the independent bounded spanning lemma (and later exact basis). For the stated levelone ranktwo e3 example the explicit JM inverse identifies H with F[T]/((T−q_H)(T+1)); q_H and −1 are distinct, so CRT gives F×F. The two normalized spectral sequences are (0,1),(0,2), as computed in the actual example. Hence each primitive block is F, whereas the whole quotient has dimension2, and its early BK image is the direct sum of the corresponding two KLR algebras. This proves both counterexample branches with the actual field/generator normalization.
